How did Russell County get its start, and why is the county seat in Phenix City?

The legislature formed the county in 1832 from land ceded by the Creek, and named it for Colonel Gilbert C. Russell. The seat has moved several times, from Girard in 1833 to Crawford in 1839, then to Seale in 1868, and finally to Phenix City in 1935.

Girard later merged into Phenix City, in 1923. The old seats still have names on the map: Crawford and Seale are unincorporated communities today, and both are outside Phenix City.

Phenix City had a hard stretch in the 1940s and 1950s, when organized crime and corruption took hold. After the 1954 killing of Albert Patterson, who had won the Democratic nomination for state attorney general on a clean-up platform, Governor Gordon Persons declared martial law on July 22, 1954. Civilian control returned on January 17, 1955.

How does the Georgia line shape Russell County?

Wikipedia reports that Russell County has the highest share in the nation of residents who work in another state, over 54%, and that most of them work in Columbus, Georgia.

  • Phenix City unofficially keeps Eastern time even though Alabama is on Central time. The county's own website lists many events with an ET tag.
  • U.S. 80 and U.S. 280 run toward Columbus, and U.S. 431 and several state routes also serve the county.
  • Wikipedia lists the Phenix City Express as local transit.

Where a house sits relative to Phenix City and the Georgia line matters to anyone who commutes, so say so plainly when you describe a property in Hurtsboro or the rural south.

Which communities and schools are in Russell County?

Phenix City is the only city, Hurtsboro is the one town, and Ladonia is a census-designated place. The unincorporated list is long: Cottonton, Crawford, Fort Mitchell, Glenville, Hatchechubbee, Holy Trinity, Hooks, Jernigan, Mahrt, Pittsview, Sandfort, Seale, Uchee and Wende.

Wikipedia lists the Russell County School District for the county. School boundaries follow addresses, so confirm the district for a specific house before you compare properties.

The county's official site points to the Chattahoochee Indian Heritage Center and the Fort Mitchell National Historic Landmark as local attractions. It also describes the Chattahoochee River for kayaking and fishing, and the Eufaula National Wildlife Refuge reaches into the county. A house near the river or refuge is worth checking with an insurer for flood questions.

What did the 2020 census show about Russell County households?

There were 23,997 households in Russell County in 2020, in 27,253 housing units. Of the occupied units, 57.1% were owner-occupied and 42.9% were rented.

Measure, 2020 censusRussell County

The population grew 11.8% between 2010 and 2020, from 52,947 to 59,183, and the 2025 estimate shows a small step back to 58,898. About 40% of the county lives in rural areas, so many properties sit outside city lines.

When are Russell County property taxes due, and when is the tax sale?

Alabama property taxes are due October 1 and turn delinquent after December 31. Under the state calendar, unpaid parcels are sent to probate court in February and advertised in April.

  • October 1: taxes due.
  • January 1: delinquent.
  • February: sent to probate court.
  • April: advertised for sale.
  • May: tax sale.

The Russell County website lists a Revenue Commissioner's delinquent tax sale held May 5, 2026, with registration due by 9:30 am Eastern. It also lists an October 14, 2026 notice from the Revenue Office about property taxes. The county courthouse is at 1000 Broad Street in Phenix City. Check the county site for the current notice before you rely on any date, since mailing and payment details can change from year to year.

Is Russell County planning for growth?

The county has been collecting public input on a long-range plan. Its website carries a September 8, 2026 notice for Russell County Comprehensive Plan 2050 meetings, inviting residents to speak up.

A plan like that can shape zoning, roads and utilities over the coming decades, so owners of land outside Phenix City may want to watch the meetings. The same site also lists a public meeting on pickleball in Fort Mitchell and an alert system for emergencies, signs of a county that is active in its smaller communities.

What homestead exemptions are available to Russell County owners?

A homestead exemption reduces the taxable value of a single-family home you own and occupy as your primary residence on the first day of the tax year, on up to 160 acres. You apply through the county office.

  • Under 65: up to $4,000 of assessed value off the state tax and up to $2,000 off the county tax.
  • Age 65 or older with income at or under $12,000 on the combined federal return: exempt from all ad valorem taxes (type H-3).
  • Permanently and totally disabled: exempt from all ad valorem taxes, with no income limit (also H-3).
  • Age 65 or older with higher income: exempt from the state portion, plus the regular $2,000 county exemption (H-4).

The exemption is tied to the owner. When a house sells, the next owner has to apply.

What does the deed tax cost when a Russell County house sells?

The deed tax is 50 cents per $500 of value, set by Alabama Code 40-22-1, and it is collected when the probate judge's office records the deed. A sale at $150,000 works out to 300 units of $500, so $150 in tax.

The statute requires proof of the real price paid, and it allows the taxable amount to drop by a mortgage on which mortgage tax was already paid. Deeds made for nominal consideration to fix a title defect are excluded. One third of the tax goes to the county treasury and two thirds to the state.

What do Russell County sellers face, and where does a cash sale fit?

Sellers here often own a house inherited from family, a rental with tenants, or a property where repairs have piled up. The Columbus commute market is steady, but older houses still need money to list well.

Cash Home Buyers reviews Russell County houses as they stand, from Phenix City neighborhoods to Seale, Crawford and Hurtsboro, and replies with a written offer. A cash closing can skip appraisals tied to a buyer's loan, and you can ask about timing that fits a tax deadline or a move.

Phenix City is in Russell County, Alabama, and it is the county seat. A small part of the city lies in Lee County.

October 1. They become delinquent after December 31, and unpaid parcels follow the state schedule toward a May tax sale.

How much is the deed tax in Russell County?

It is 50 cents for each $500 of value conveyed, under Alabama Code 40-22-1. The probate judge's office collects it when the deed is recorded.

Does Russell County use Eastern or Central time?

Alabama is officially on Central time, but Phenix City unofficially uses Eastern time. The county website lists events with an ET tag.

Dekalb County by the numbers

Where is DeKalb County, Alabama?

DeKalb County fills the northeast corner of Alabama, up against the Georgia line. Its county commission calls it the Northeast Gateway to Alabama and puts the area at 784 square miles, while the Census Bureau figure quoted by Wikipedia is 779.

Fort Payne is the county seat and the largest city. Jackson County lies to the north, Marshall County to the west, Etowah County to the south and Cherokee County to the southeast. Three Georgia counties (Dade, Walker and Chattooga) touch the eastern edge.

The county is part of the Huntsville-Decatur-Albertville combined statistical area, so many residents live in DeKalb and work in a neighboring county.

How did DeKalb County begin?

The Alabama legislature created DeKalb County on January 9, 1836, from land the Cherokee Nation gave up under duress before its forced removal west. The county carries the name of Major General Baron Johann de Kalb, an American Revolution figure.

Fort Payne grew around a fort of the same name, which was built in the 1830s to hold Cherokee people before removal. Sequoyah, who created the Cherokee syllabary, lived in this area in the early 1800s. Wikipedia also notes that DeKalb is largely a dry county for alcohol sales, though Fort Payne voted in 2005 to allow them and Rainsville, Collinsville and Henagar later followed.

How fast has DeKalb County grown?

DeKalb County added about 6,600 people between the 2000 and 2010 censuses, then nearly stood still through 2020. Wikipedia lists 64,452 residents in 2000, 71,109 in 2010 and 71,608 in 2020, with a 2025 estimate of 74,085.

The Hispanic or Latino share of the population rose from 5.55 percent in 2000 to 13.63 percent in 2010 and 16.4 percent in 2020. Population stood at 45,048 in 1950 and first passed 53,000 in the 1980 census.

The 2020 census counted 30,584 housing units for 27,145 households, which leaves roughly 3,400 units vacant. An empty house still carries a full tax bill each October.

What are the key numbers for DeKalb County housing?

The 2020 census counted 71,608 people in DeKalb County, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 74,085, a gain of 3.5 percent. Homeownership is high and most of the county is rural.

These figures come from the Wikipedia county article, which reports 2020 census data. With nearly nine in ten residents living in rural areas, many DeKalb houses sit on acreage instead of city lots.

What towns and cities are in DeKalb County?

DeKalb County has three cities and seventeen towns. Fort Payne, Henagar and Rainsville are the cities.

  • Towns: Collinsville (partly in Cherokee County), Crossville, Fyffe, Geraldine, Hammondville, Ider, Kilpatrick, Lakeview, Mentone, Pine Ridge, Powell, Sand Rock, Shiloh, Sylvania and Valley Head.
  • Unincorporated places include Sulphur Springs, Grove Oak, Dawson and Whiton.
  • Part of Little River Canyon National Preserve lies inside the county.

A seller in a small town may deal with different utilities and code officers than a seller in Fort Payne, so the first call is to the town hall.

What roads and rail serve DeKalb County?

Interstate 59 crosses the county, and U.S. 11 is the other major route. State routes 35, 40, 68, 75, 117, 168, 176 and 227 link the smaller towns.

Norfolk Southern Railway also runs through the county.

What weather events have damaged DeKalb County homes?

DeKalb County has a documented record of severe events that matter when a buyer inspects a house. Wikipedia lists two in this century.

  • April 29, 2003: a magnitude 4.6 earthquake with an epicenter on the county's eastern edge cracked foundations, and one chimney fell.
  • April 27, 2011: the Super Outbreak caused 31 deaths in the county, 25 of them from the Rainsville tornado, which was an EF5.

A house with older storm repairs, a cracked foundation or a patched roof can still sell, but it often needs a buyer who is willing to take it without a long repair negotiation.

How is property classified for tax in Alabama?

Alabama sets assessment ratios by class, and the ratio decides what share of market value gets taxed. Etowah County's published FAQ lists the four classes, which apply statewide.

ClassType of propertyAssessment ratio
IUtilities30%
IIAll other property20%
IIIFarm, forest and owner-occupied10%
IVMotor vehicles15%

An owner-occupied house in DeKalb County is taxed at the lower Class III ratio. A rental house falls into the 20 percent class, so a landlord's bill on the same value is about double.

When are DeKalb County property taxes due?

Taxes are due October 1 and turn delinquent after December 31, per the Alabama Department of Revenue. The state timetable then runs to a tax sale in May.

  • October 1: due
  • January 1: delinquent
  • February: turned over to Probate Court
  • March: Probate Court meets
  • April: advertised for sale
  • May: tax sale

The DeKalb County commission site did not post office or payment details that could be confirmed here, so a seller should call the county Revenue Commissioner's office in Fort Payne for the exact payoff and the office hours.

What does a DeKalb County deed cost to record?

The recording privilege tax is fifty cents for each $500 of value, set by Alabama Code section 40-22-1. The probate office collects it when the deed goes on record.

The buyer or seller must show the actual purchase price on a Department of Revenue form. On a $120,000 sale that is 240 units of $500, so the tax is $120 plus the probate recording fee. The state keeps two-thirds and the county one-third.

A deed with no proof of price can be taxed by the most recent assessment and carry a penalty.

What can a DeKalb County seller do about a high assessment?

A taxpayer can contest a valuation through the county Board of Equalization. A ruling from that board can be appealed to circuit court.

Section 40-3-25 of the 2022 Alabama Code sets a 30 day window for that circuit court appeal, and it requires the taxpayer to keep paying the tax in the meantime. The code on Justia notes a newer version exists, so confirm current rules with the Revenue Commissioner.

What problems do DeKalb County sellers usually bring?

Rural acreage and older mountain houses create their own difficulties.

  • An inherited house on land with several years of unpaid taxes
  • A rental with a Class II assessment and a tenant who has left
  • Storm or foundation damage that makes financing hard for a retail buyer
  • A property on a private or mountain road that few agents want to show

A cash buyer can look at the house as it stands, pay the back taxes from the sale, and close on the seller's timeline.

More questions about DeKalb County, AL Property Tax Guide

Fort Payne is the county seat and the largest city, according to Wikipedia.

What is the property tax assessment ratio for a home in DeKalb County?

An owner-occupied home falls in Class III at 10 percent of value. Other property, including most rentals, is Class II at 20 percent, per the class table published by Etowah County for Alabama.

When do DeKalb County property taxes become delinquent?

After December 31, with the January 1 delinquency date followed by a May tax sale, according to the Alabama Department of Revenue.

How much is the deed recording tax in DeKalb County?

Fifty cents for each $500 of value under Alabama Code 40-22-1. A $120,000 sale carries $120 in tax, plus the probate recording fee.

Can I sell a DeKalb County house that has unpaid taxes?

Yes. The unpaid balance is normally paid from the sale proceeds at closing, because Alabama taxes follow the property.

St Clair County by the numbers

Why does St. Clair County have two county seats?

St. Clair County has two seats, Ashville and Pell City, because the mountains split the county in two. Wikipedia's county entry explains that the far southern end of the Appalachians runs northeast to southwest through the county, which made it hard to administer from one side, so Pell City was added to serve the southeast.

Alabama has only two counties with more than one seat, and the United States has 33. For a property owner, this matters because county business can happen in either town. When you call about a tax record, ask which office handles your parcel and whether you need to go in person.

We could not open the St. Clair County government pages, so we cannot give office addresses, hours or the name of the current revenue commissioner. Check the county's own site or phone the commissioner's office before you drive anywhere.

Where is St. Clair County and how did it form?

St. Clair County is in central Alabama and is part of the Birmingham metropolitan area. It covers 654 square miles, of which 632 are land, and Pell City is its largest city.

The Alabama Territory legislature created the county on November 20, 1818 by splitting land from Shelby County, and named it for General Arthur St. Clair. Parts of it were later used to form Cherokee and DeKalb Counties in 1836 and Etowah County in 1866. In 2019 it became the seventh Alabama county to adopt its own flag.

Neighbors are Etowah County to the northeast, Calhoun to the east, Talladega to the southeast, Shelby to the southwest, Jefferson to the west and Blount to the northwest.

What do the county's population and housing numbers show?

St. Clair County had 91,103 residents in 2020, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 98,206. The county has grown at every count since 1980, when it had 41,205 people.

Measure (2020 census)St. Clair County
Population91,103

Renter-occupied homes18.8% of occupied units

The rural share is the figure to keep in mind: 67.1 percent of residents lived outside urban areas in 2020. The census also put the homeowner vacancy rate at 1.2 percent and the rental vacancy rate at 7.6 percent. A property's tax bill depends on whether it falls inside a city and which taxing districts apply, so check the parcel, not the mailing town.

When are St. Clair County property taxes due?

The Alabama Department of Revenue says property taxes are due October 1 and are delinquent after December 31. The same timetable lists the next steps for an unpaid bill: delinquency on January 1, a turnover to probate court in February, a court meeting in March, advertising in April and a tax sale in May.

Counties do not have to mail a notice. The Revenue Commissioner's office sends one as a courtesy, so a missing bill does not cancel the debt. If you own a St. Clair County house you have not visited in a while, call the office and ask what, if anything, is owed.

  • October 1: taxes due
  • December 31: last day to pay without delinquency, and the reporting deadline for improvements
  • January 1: taxes delinquent
  • February to May: probate court steps toward a tax sale

How is a St. Clair County house assessed, and what changes it?

The assessed value comes from an appraised value, and the department's example applies a 10 percent assessment rate to $100,000 to get $10,000 before the millage rate is applied. A bill rises when the millage rises or when the appraised value goes up through reappraisal or the market.

Every Alabama county now reviews a quarter of its parcels each year under annual equalization, so a full review comes around every four years. The state says this produces smaller yearly changes than the old four-year jumps.

If you build onto a house, owners must sign a new assessment at the Revenue Commissioner's office by December 31 for work finished by October 1. The department lists additions, pools, remodeling, an added bath, deck, patio, carport or garage as reportable. Re-roofing and painting are not.

Who qualifies for a homestead exemption in St. Clair County?

An owner-occupied single-family home on up to 160 acres can qualify, if the owner lived in it on the first day of the tax year. The state exempts owners over 65, permanently and totally disabled owners and blind owners from the state share of the tax, while county taxes can still be due.

In the 2020 census, 17.4 percent of St. Clair County residents were 65 or older, so the age-based exemption touches a large share of owners. A family selling a parent's house should find out whether a claim was on file, since the state share of the bill depends on it. You apply at the local county office. Because we could not open St. Clair's pages, we are not quoting any county-level exemption amounts. If you inherited a house from an owner who had an exemption, ask the office what you need to file.

What should buyers and sellers do about St. Clair County property tax?

The state says a buyer should record the deed in the probate office and then assess the property at the revenue commissioner's office, bringing the deed. A bill may still carry the former owner's name, and the owner of the property answers for the tax anyway.

Sellers should do three things before closing:

  • Ask which year's tax is paid and whether any balance remains.
  • Write into the contract who pays the current year's tax.
  • Report any address change to the county office in writing.

We could not confirm the St. Clair County appeal procedure or deadline from an official page, so ask the revenue commissioner's office how to contest a value before you list.

What roads and places matter to a St. Clair County seller?

Interstate 20 and Interstate 59 cross the county, along with U.S. 11, 78, 231 and 411 and several state routes.

Logan Martin Lake and Horse Pens 40, a private park on Chandler Mountain, are the places Wikipedia highlights. The county's school system is the St. Clair County School District. Trussville, Leeds, Springville, Moody, Margaret and Odenville are among the cities and towns, and some, like Trussville and Leeds, are mostly in other counties.

A cash purchase does not change the tax steps above. We buy the house as it stands, and the deed, taxes and recording are handled the same way as in any sale.

More questions about St. Clair County, AL Property Tax Guide

When are St. Clair County, Alabama property taxes due?

October 1, with delinquency after December 31, according to the Alabama Department of Revenue. Unpaid bills can move to a probate court tax sale in May.

Why are there two county seats in St. Clair County?

Ashville and Pell City are both county seats because the Appalachian terrain divides the county, and a second seat was set up in Pell City to serve the southeast side.

Do I owe tax if I never received a bill?

Yes. The state says the revenue commissioner is not required to mail notices, and the owner is responsible whether or not a statement arrives.

Do I have to report improvements to my St. Clair County house?

Yes, for additions, new structures, pools, remodeling and similar work done by October 1. Sign a new assessment at the revenue commissioner's office by December 31. Re-roofing and painting do not need one.
